comment: Shared scripted round traces. The native Desktop round driver
(apps/desktop/src/plugins/hermes-bots/group-rounds.ts, driven through group-test-utils'
scripted gateway) and the hosted-room policy (gateway/hosted_room_discussion.py, driven
through its planner and checkpoint on an isolated store) both run these exact scripts.
Each scenario compares the COMPLETE ordered speaker trace, not a first responder or a count,
plus the input delta a resumed member actually receives.
'user' messages are sent one at a time, each drive awaited before the next. 'replies' gives
each member's scripted answers in order; a member that runs out of lines passes.
'speakers' is the ordered list of committed member messages. Handles equal member names so
both mention resolvers address the same members.

scenarios.name: unmentioned discussion keeps both members answering later rounds
comment: Round 0 dispatches the rotated roster a,b. Round 1 rotates to b,a: b has no new delta
after its own last reply and is skipped at group-rounds.ts:573-579, so a answers b.
Round 2 rotates back to a,b and the same rule skips a. The round cap ends the drive.
Hosted settles after round 0 today: that is the participation gap this pins.

scenarios.name: a peer handoff lets the original member answer the substantive reply

b: B substantive answer with no mention

scenarios.name: a held member does not take the slot rotation gives it

a: A must never speak while held

scenarios.name: a released member still sees the context addressed to its peer
a citation nobody answered still owes a turn when a later round goes quiet
comment: The first discussion leaves a's citation of b unresolved because b says nothing. The
second same-thread message addresses only a, whose ordinary round then has nothing to
say. Recovery drives the cited member; here it passes too, so the room settles.
'replies' is keyed by user message so b's script cannot be consumed by the first
discussion's turns.

scenarios.name: a productive recovery answers the old citation and the room continues
comment_dispatch: The recovery turn is productive, so the drive does not settle on it: an ordinary round
follows and offers the turn back to a, which now has the new answer in its delta.

scenarios.name: a held member owed a recovery turn is skipped by both engines
comment: b is paused, cited by a peer, and then owed a recovery turn when a later round goes
quiet. Neither engine may give it that turn while the hold stands.

scenarios.name: a broadcast reply leaves no handoff for either engine to recover
comment: The accepted old-citation recovery shape with the citation replaced by `@all`: if a
broadcast were read as citing everyone, the quiet second discussion would dispatch a
recovery turn exactly where the explicit-citation vector does.
